findings.title: i18next placeholder syntax broken by Java-style MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat substitution
findings.body: This file is consumed by the React account-ui app via react-i18next, which requires double-curly-brace interpolation syntax (`{{0}}`). The change replaces `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` with `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, which uses single braces and Java's MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax. i18next will not interpret `{0}` as a variable and has no understanding of `{2,choice,...}`, so this message will render literally/unsubstituted (or broken) in the Account Console UI instead of being correctly interpolated. The same regression is applied to the admin-ui translation file.

findings.title: i18next placeholder syntax broken in admin-ui translations
findings.body: Same issue as in account-ui: `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This file is consumed by the React admin-ui through react-i18next, which uses `{{var}}` double-brace syntax, not Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat. The new text will not be correctly interpolated in the Admin Console, showing raw/unsubstituted template text to users.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `totpStep1` for the Lithuanian locale was changed from a valid (if HTML-containing) Lithuanian sentence to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy/paste mistake made while stripping disallowed anchor tags from the translation, resulting in Lithuanian users seeing Italian text instead of their own language.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `loginTotpStep1` for the Lithuanian login theme was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian text, not a Lithuanian translation. This is the same mistake as in the account theme's `messages_lt.properties` and will show Lithuanian users an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup screen.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws unchecked RuntimeException instead of the declared MojoExecutionException
findings.body: verify() declares `throws MojoExecutionException` and only catches IOException from the duplicate-key check, but verifySafeHtml() wraps its own IOExceptions (reading the file or the derived English reference file) in `RuntimeException`. These RuntimeExceptions are not caught anywhere in verify(), so they propagate uncaught out of the public API, producing an unhandled exception/raw stack trace during the Maven build instead of the clean MojoExecutionException the method contract promises, and aborting the whole verification run rather than reporting it as a verification failure for that file.

findings.title: Fragile, unguarded derivation of the English reference file path
findings.body: The English counterpart file path is derived purely via two chained `String.replaceAll` calls on the absolute path (`resources-community`->`resources`, and the locale suffix ->`_en.properties`). If this heuristic fails to produce an existing file (e.g. non-standard directory layouts, or a locale file whose English source doesn't live where the heuristic expects), the subsequent `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws an IOException that is converted into an uncaught RuntimeException (see other finding), crashing the whole verification run instead of reporting a specific, actionable error for that file.

findings.title: Anchor-tag comparison assumes identical ordering between translation and English source
findings.body: santizeAnchors() walks through ``/`` matches in the translated value and the English value in lockstep (sequential `find()` calls), requiring the Nth anchor tag in the translation to equal the Nth anchor tag in English. Translations that legitimately reorder anchor tags (common due to different grammar/word order) will trigger a false 'Didn't find anchor tag' verification failure even though the same tags are present, just in a different order, causing legitimate translations to fail CI/build verification.

findings.title: HTML detection regex misses uppercase and closing tags
findings.body: `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches lowercase opening tags. English source strings whose only HTML markers are closing tags (e.g. ``) or use uppercase tag names will be judged as not containing HTML by containsHtml(), causing the stricter POLICY_NO_HTML to be applied to translations even when the English source itself is HTML-bearing, which can produce confusing or incorrect verification results.

findings.title: No tests for normalizeValue special-case branches or the happy-path (valid translation) scenario
findings.body: normalizeValue() contains several non-trivial special-case branches (templateHelp's `CLAIM.<NAME>` allowance, optimizeLookupHelp's `<Extensions>` allowance, linkExpirationFormatter/error-invalid-multivalued-size ChoiceFormat stripping, and email RTL style stripping), none of which are covered by any test. There is also no test confirming that a well-formed translation containing legitimate allowed HTML/anchors passes verification without reporting any messages, so regressions in these code paths (e.g. the i18next-breaking change found in account-ui/admin-ui files) would not be caught by this test suite.
